summary: Deliver the pinned OpenAPI comparison capability in four dependency-ordered epics: establish report/configuration contracts, implement the isolated Git and oasdiff engine, integrate it into the CLI, then add the controlled Git-history fixture lane and operator documentation. The plan preserves the existing Python scanner behavior while upgrading reports to schema 0.3 only where OpenAPI findings require additional fields. EPIC-002 and EPIC-003 have non-overlapping write scopes after the shared-contract checkpoint, allowing the fixture lane to proceed alongside CLI integration once the comparison interface is stable.

epics.title: Freeze OpenAPI policy and report contracts
epics.description: Extend scanner configuration, policy, finding projection, and JSON Schema to define the shared OpenAPI adapter contract before comparison code is wired. Own scanner/src/dogwatch/config.py, contracts.py, openapi_policy.py, report.py, scanner/schemas/report-0.3.schema.json, and their direct tests; retain report-0.2.schema.json for historical validation.
acceptance_criteria: The policy parser accepts the approved [openapi] contracts, severity reclassification, and exact-match waiver grammar; it rejects unknown fields, duplicate policy targets, unsupported or off severities, malformed hashes/dates, and malformed operation locators through configuration diagnostics.

Schema version 0.3 retains the existing report envelope and validates existing non-OpenAPI findings unchanged, while an OpenAPI finding requires source, severity, check ID, locator, human message, fingerprint, waiver state, and base/candidate provenance.
[AC-4] Every OpenAPI finding includes severity, check ID, locator, human message, fingerprint, and base/candidate provenance.

Reclassification changes only effective severity; matched waivers preserve the finding and attached waiver metadata while removing only its gate effect, including expiry behavior under an injected evaluation date.
Report sorting, canonical serialization, status precedence, and exits continue to make an error diagnostic inconclusive before any unwaived error finding can make the report fail.

`cd scanner && uv run --locked pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_contracts.py tests/test_report.py tests/test_schema.py` passes, and `cd scanner && uv run --locked ruff format --check . && uv run --locked ruff check . && uv run --locked mypy` passes.

epics.title: Build isolated OpenAPI comparison engine
epics.description: Implement the local-only comparison boundary beneath the frozen EPIC-001 data contracts. Own openapi.py, openapi_git.py, openapi_validate.py, openapi_tool.py, scanner/scripts/install_oasdiff.py, the YAML runtime dependency and lockfile update, plus scanner/tests/openapi/test_git.py, test_validate.py, test_tool.py, and test_policy.py.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve an explicit baseline ref once to an immutable local commit, then read only the configured repository-relative path as a regular Git blob using argv-only Git calls with prompts, lazy fetch, replacement objects, and optional locks disabled; no checkout, fetch, clone, LFS, Git-revision input to oasdiff, or network access occurs during scanning.

Preflight candidate and baseline bytes independently: enforce the 5 MiB raw limit and regular-file requirements, safe-parse YAML or JSON, accept declared OpenAPI 3.0.x/3.1.x/3.2.x documents, reject malformed or unsupported documents, and reject unresolved internal or every external $ref form before the tool runs.
Add and lock a safe YAML parser in scanner/pyproject.toml and scanner/uv.lock; parsing tests demonstrate that no unsafe YAML constructors execute.

Provide `make install-oasdiff` support through the installer: select only the approved macOS, Linux amd64, or Linux arm64 v1.39.0 archive; verify its stated SHA-256; reject unsafe archive entries; atomically cache the executable in an ignored local location; and require `oasdiff --version` to report 1.39.0. The scanner itself never downloads a tool.
[AC-2] oasdiff invocation uses an argv list, pinned version, read-only temporary files, timeout/output limits, and disabled external reference loading.

The runner invokes only the approved changelog argv with stdin disconnected, private working directory and controlled environment; it concurrently caps stdout at 16 MiB and stderr at 1 MiB, terminates on either cap or the 60-second timeout, and maps each specified failure condition to its approved OpenAPI diagnostic ID.

Accepted tool JSON is normalized only when required finding identity fields are valid; malformed or incomplete tool output yields openapi-tool-failed rather than a fabricated policy finding. Fingerprints follow the approved openapi/v1 canonical-JSON contract and exclude the human message.
`cd scanner && uv run --locked pytest tests/openapi/test_git.py tests/openapi/test_validate.py tests/openapi/test_tool.py tests/openapi/test_policy.py` passes.

epics.title: Wire comparisons into scanner command
epics.description: Integrate the completed comparison engine with dogwatch check without changing API or web areas. Own scanner/src/dogwatch/cli.py and scanner/tests/test_cli.py, with the EPIC-001 report projection and EPIC-002 comparison result interface treated as fixed integration seams.
acceptance_criteria: `dogwatch check` accepts `--baseline-ref REF`; when one or more OpenAPI Contract Declarations are loaded, omission of that argument produces an OpenAPI error diagnostic in the emitted schema-0.3 report and exit 2 rather than an argparse-only or policy-failure result.
[AC-1] The adapter compares the configured candidate contract with the same path from an explicit baseline Git ref.

Each configured declaration runs as one independent bounded comparison, using the resolved baseline commit and candidate path/hash in its provenance; normal OpenAPI findings combine deterministically with existing scanner findings and diagnostics.
[AC-3] No-change contracts yield a successful report with no OpenAPI findings; invalid/missing inputs and tool failures yield diagnostics rather than false policy failures.

Missing candidate or baseline files, unavailable/invalid refs, validation failures, unavailable tool, timeout, output-limit conditions, non-zero tool exits, and malformed tool output produce only the declared OpenAPI diagnostics; their error severity yields inconclusive and exit 2.

CLI tests cover baseline argument behavior, schema-0.3 output, stdout/file output, deterministic diagnostic rendering, pass/fail/inconclusive exit mapping, and retain the existing no-OpenAPI command behavior.
`cd scanner && uv run --locked pytest tests/test_cli.py tests/test_report.py tests/test_schema.py` passes.

epics.title: Add deterministic fixture verification lane
epics.description: Create the dedicated OpenAPI compatibility fixture harness and pinned artifacts, then expose the supported bootstrap and verification workflow. Own fixtures/openapi/**, scanner/tests/openapi/test_fixtures.py, harness.py, regenerate.py, fake_oasdiff.py, Makefile, README.md, fixtures/README.md, .gitignore, and any necessary scanner golden-harness adjustments; do not change normalization logic or shared schemas.
acceptance_criteria: The harness materializes each `base/` and `candidate/` case into a temporary local Git repository, commits the baseline, supplies an explicit baseline ref, and records only deterministic report bytes, exit code, and controlled invocation evidence.
[AC-5] The researched fixture matrix is covered by automated tests using pinned expected outputs.

The named matrix includes no-change, removals, requiredness, enum/constraint breaks, invalid input, missing input, timeout, tool failure, and ignored or reclassified findings; timeout and tool-failure cases use the controlled substitute executable rather than a wall-clock or upstream failure.

Golden reports validate against report-0.3, assert required provenance and stable fingerprints where findings exist, preserve waived findings, and repeated runs produce byte-identical serialized reports. Fixture tests never regenerate expected outputs implicitly.

Existing scanner-wide fixtures remain pass fixtures: their harness supplies an explicit local baseline when a fixture declares an OpenAPI contract, and their schema/golden expectations move consistently to 0.3 without embedding environment-specific paths or commits.

Makefile exposes verified-tool bootstrap and fixture-test wiring; README documents supported macOS/Linux bootstrap, cache behavior, `--baseline-ref` usage, and the fact that scans never download tools. fixtures/README documents the Git-history layout and explicit OpenAPI golden regeneration process.
After a verified local oasdiff cache is available, `make test-scanner`, `make test-fixtures`, and `make lint-scanner` pass from the repository root.

risk_notes: The workspace is already dirty in .am/runtime-pointer.json, .gitignore, and .idea/; implementation must preserve unrelated changes, especially because EPIC-004 legitimately edits .gitignore.

The real compatibility fixtures require the verified local v1.39.0 cache. `make install-oasdiff` may need access to the fixed upstream release during initial bootstrap, while scanner execution must remain offline.

The existing full-surface fixture already declares an OpenAPI contract but its current golden harness supplies no baseline ref. EPIC-004 must update that harness deterministically so the existing pass fixture continues to validate the new mandatory-baseline behavior.
Only macOS and Linux are in scope; installer and fixture coverage must reject or clearly diagnose unsupported platforms rather than implying Windows support.
verification_strategy: Run contract/unit checks at each epic boundary, then execute the end-to-end matrix from the repository root: `make test-scanner`, `make test-fixtures`, and `make lint-scanner`. The fixture lane is the integration proof: it uses temporary committed Git histories, the pinned/verified oasdiff path for normal comparisons, the controlled executable for failure boundaries, schema validation for every pinned report, invocation-safety assertions, and repeated-run byte equality.
